Find PTM-PTM pairs within one dataset, with mzLib's PtmPairEngine

ptmqtl_pairs.Rd

PTM-PTM pairs within one dataset: two modifications identified together on one peptidoform (physical), and two sites whose occupancies rise and fall together across runs (co-varying), with Benjamini-Hochberg q-values.

Two kinds of evidence, which you choose between with type:

Usage

ptmqtl_pairs(observations, type, samples = NULL, modifications = NULL,
  categories = NULL, min_quantified_fraction = NULL, keep_ceiling = FALSE,
  include_bounds = FALSE, run_covariate = NULL, remove_run_level = FALSE,
  run_level_group = NULL, run_level_groups = NULL, timeout = 600)

Arguments

observations

ptmqtl_occupancy's observations table, with the same rules.

type

"physical", "covarying" or "both" (physical rows first). Required: mzLib has no default between its two methods.

samples

ptmqtl_occupancy's run-to-sample table; pairs are then across samples.

modifications

As ptmqtl_occupancy: only these modifications are sites.

categories

As ptmqtl_occupancy: only these categories are sites.

min_quantified_fraction

Co-varying only. A site enters pairs only if quantified in at least this fraction of the runs (fraction of the runs, above 0 and at most 1), rounded up. NULL: mzLib's default (0.7 at mzLib d10017ce), which min_quantified_fraction in the result reports.

keep_ceiling

Co-varying only. Keep runs where a site was seen only modified. FALSE sends nothing, so mzLib's default (leave them out) applies.

include_bounds

Co-varying only. Let a run where a site was seen in only one form enter as a tied bound, never an invented value (mzLib #1468): "not_detected" and "floor" cells rank below every fraction of the site, ceilings and count-only cells seen only modified above. A site often below detection can then be tested at all. A pair whose two sites are both mostly one bound is not tested ("both_sites_mostly_bounds"). FALSE (the default) sends nothing: mzLib's default, no bounds.

run_covariate

Co-varying only. A TSV with a header row whose second field names the covariate (e.g. target_psms), then run, value: each run's depth, or any per-run value, in any unit. Pairs become the partial Spearman correlation given it (mzLib #1468); it is ranked, so log2 gives the same answer. Leave a run out for "unknown"; it is then left out of every pair. mzLib refuses a value that is not finite. NULL (the default): no covariate.

remove_run_level

Co-varying only. Correlate given each run's level - the median occupancy of the other tested sites of the pair's group - to remove a batch or loading shift. Batch only: where the level follows the design, it removes the effect you study.

run_level_group

With remove_run_level: "category" or "modification", for one level per group of sites. NULL: one level for every site, mzLib's default. Not with run_level_groups.

run_level_groups

With remove_run_level: a TSV with a header row, then modification, group, for any grouping, such as chemistry. Every modification among the sites needs a group.

timeout

Seconds to allow, or NULL to wait indefinitely.

Details

- physical (PtmPairEngine.Physical): both modifications were identified on one peptidoform, so on one molecule. statistic is the median co-occupancy over the runs where both were quantified. There is no test. - covarying (PtmPairEngine.CoVarying): the two sites' occupancies rise and fall together (or oppositely) across runs. statistic is Spearman's rho on the runs where both are quantified, with a Benjamini-Hochberg q per family. Floors, undetected cells and, by default, ceilings are left out: two unrelated sites both read 1 in low-load runs, which would correlate them through detection alone. include_bounds = TRUE lets them in as tied bounds instead, and run_covariate correlates given each run's depth.

Occupancy is computed inside by the same mzLib call ptmqtl_occupancy makes.

Value

An mzlibr_ptm_pairs:

- records, a data.frame with one row per pair of sites, physical pairs first: result_type, "physical" (both on one peptidoform) or "covarying" (across runs); site_a and site_b, the two sites' keys, site_a first by ordinal order; same_protein; overlapping, one peptide covers both (such a co-varying pair is correlated by construction); statistic (physical: fraction (0 to 1), the median co-occupancy; covarying: unitless correlation (-1 to 1), Spearman's rho), NA when physical pairs were never quantified together, or not tested; p_value, a fraction (0 to 1), two-sided Spearman, NA for physical (no test) or not tested; q, a fraction (0 to 1), Benjamini-Hochberg within fdr_family, NA when not in the family (physical, overlapping, not tested), not a target-decoy q-value; fdr_family, P or A then intra or inter protein, e.g. "A:inter"; n (runs), physical: runs identified together, covarying: runs where both sites have a value; statistic_n (runs), the runs statistic was computed on; spearman_method, "exact", "asymptotic" or "not_estimable" (every untested pair), NA for physical; run_level_removed; test_status, mzLib's PairTestStatus (#1468): "tested", or why not - "not_estimable", "too_few_shared_runs" or "both_sites_mostly_bounds" - NA for physical; and bounds_included and run_covariate_removed, whether one-form cells entered as tied bounds (include_bounds) and whether rho is partial given the run covariate (run_covariate), always FALSE for physical. - observations_file, samples_file and run_level_groups_file (NA when not given), as absolute paths; type; observation_count rows read; run_count runs; sample_count samples, NA without samples; run_names; and, NA for type = "physical": covarying_run_count (runs), the runs where any site was identified or covered, the denominator of min_quantified_fraction (fraction of the runs, 0 to 1), the guard used; exclude_ceiling, FALSE with keep_ceiling = TRUE and NA when you did not choose (mzLib decides inside PtmPairEngine.CoVarying, and leaves ceilings out; mzLib #1468); include_bounds, whether one-form cells entered as tied bounds, yours or mzLib's default (FALSE); remove_run_level; run_level_group, "none", "category", "modification" or "file", NA when the run level was not removed; min_runs_for_run_level (runs), with the run level or a run covariate removed, the fewest shared runs a pair is tested on (fewer is "too_few_shared_runs"), and min_sites_for_run_level (sites), the fewest other sites a run's group needs to have a level, mzLib's thresholds, NA when not removed; min_untied_share (fraction of the shared runs, 0 to 1), mzLib's guard with bounds - a pair is tested only if one of its sites has at least this share of the shared runs outside its largest tie - NA without bounds; run_covariate_file (absolute path) and run_covariate_name (the covariate table's second header), NA without a run covariate; run_covariate_runs_missing, the runs (or samples) with no covariate value, left out of every pair, empty when every run has one and NULL without a run covariate; modifications and categories, NULL for no filter; ignored_columns; physical_count pairs (NA for "covarying") and covarying_count pairs (NA for "physical"); row_count rows; column_names. - caveats: what each pair type means, and the run level when it was removed, plus any that apply to this input.

Wraps

Wire verb ptmqtl pairs. Generated from the bridge's verb spec ptmqtl.pairs.yaml (bridge commit aea14604d5f7) by scripts/build-man.R; the spec owns these facts, and all three bindings render the same ones.

  • PtmPairEngine.Physical in mzLib/Quantification/PtmQtl/PtmPairs.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • PtmPairEngine.CoVarying in mzLib/Quantification/PtmQtl/PtmPairs.cs at mzLib cc67b7a2

  • PtmPairEngine.DefaultMinQuantifiedFraction in mzLib/Quantification/PtmQtl/PtmPairs.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • PtmPairEngine.MinRunsForRunLevel in mzLib/Quantification/PtmQtl/PtmPairs.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • PtmPairEngine.MinSitesForRunLevel in mzLib/Quantification/PtmQtl/PtmPairs.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • PtmPairEngine.MinUntiedShare in mzLib/Quantification/PtmQtl/PtmPairs.cs at mzLib cc67b7a2

  • PtmPair in mzLib/Quantification/PtmQtl/PtmPairs.cs at mzLib cc67b7a2

  • PairTestStatus in mzLib/Quantification/PtmQtl/PtmPairs.cs at mzLib cc67b7a2

  • SiteOccupancyCalculator.Calculate in mzLib/Quantification/PtmQtl/SiteOccupancy.cs at mzLib d10017ce

  • SiteOccupancyCalculator.CombineObservations in mzLib/Quantification/PtmQtl/SiteOccupancy.cs at mzLib d10017ce

Parameters: units, ranges and defaults

observations

path; required. ptmqtl occupancy's observations table, with the same rules: a header row naming run, full_sequence, protein_accession, start_residue, end_residue (1-based), intensity (instrument units; blank, NA or NaN is identified but not quantified) and optionally previous_residue; one row per (run, peptidoform, protein), MS/MS identifications only.

type

string; required; range physical | covarying | both. Which pairs: physical (PtmPairEngine.Physical, mzLib's type P), covarying (PtmPairEngine.CoVarying, type A), or both, physical rows first. Required: they are different evidence, and mzLib has no default between its two methods.

samples

path; default absent. Optional. ptmqtl occupancy's run-to-sample table (a header row, then run, sample). With it the observations are first combined per sample by mzLib's CombineObservations, so both pair types are computed across samples rather than fractions. Map only fractions together. Absent, none is sent: pairs are across runs.

modifications

string; default absent; range exact names, tab-separated, none blank. Optional. As ptmqtl occupancy: count only these modifications (Category:IdWithMotif, separated by tabs) as sites. Not with categories. Absent, no filter.

categories

string; default absent; range category names, tab-separated, none blank. Optional. As ptmqtl occupancy: count only modifications of these categories. Not with modifications. Absent, no filter.

min_quantified_fraction (wire --min-quantified-fraction)

float; in fraction of the runs (0 to 1); default mzLib's PtmPairEngine.DefaultMinQuantifiedFraction, 0.7 at the pin; range > 0 and <= 1. Co-varying only. A site enters co-varying pairs only if its occupancy is quantified (a ceiling counts only with keep-ceiling) in at least this fraction of the runs, rounded up: the runs (or samples) where any site was identified or covered, reported as covarying_run_count. Absent, the bridge sends none and mzLib's default applies.

keep_ceiling (wire --keep-ceiling)

flag; default absent: null is sent, and mzLib's CoVarying resolves its nullable excludeCeiling itself (ceilings left out). Co-varying only. Keep a run where a site was seen only modified (a fraction of 1 with unmodified_quantified false). Two unrelated sites both read 1 in low-load runs, so ceilings can correlate sites through detection alone; mzLib leaves them out unless asked. With include-bounds it sends false, which mzLib accepts: a ceiling is then a high bound either way.

include_bounds (wire --include-bounds)

flag; default absent: mzLib's includeBounds default, false at the pin, so one-form cells are left out. Co-varying only. Let a run where a site was seen in only one form enter as a bound, never as an invented value (mzLib's includeBounds, #1468): not_detected (a covered-zero) and floor cells tie below every fraction of that site; a ceiling, or a count_only cell whose covering peptidoforms all carry the modification, ties above every fraction. A count_only cell where both forms were identified has no rank and is left out. Bounds count toward min-quantified-fraction and toward a run's level. A pair whose two sites are both mostly one bound is not tested (both_sites_mostly_bounds). The bridge never sends excludeCeiling true, so mzLib's refusal of the two together cannot arise from this verb.

run_covariate (wire --run-covariate)

path; default absent. Co-varying only. A TSV with a header row whose second field names the covariate (for example target_psms), then run, value: one row per run (or with samples, per sample), in any unit. Pairs are then the partial Spearman correlation given it (mzLib's runCovariate, #1468), for example the run's depth: shallow runs make covered-zeros co-occur across unrelated sites. It is ranked, so any increasing transform (log2) gives the same result. A run left out of the file is left out of every pair; a blank, NA or NaN value is sent as NaN and mzLib refuses it (leave the run out instead). Absent, none is sent.

remove_run_level (wire --remove-run-level)

flag; default absent: mzLib's removeRunLevel default, false at the pin. Co-varying only. Correlate given each run's level: the partial Spearman correlation with the run's median occupancy over the other tested sites of the pair's group (the pair's own two left out). Removes a batch or loading shift that moves many sites in the same runs. Batch only: where the run level follows the design, removing it tests the correlation within conditions instead.

run_level_group (wire --run-level-group)

string; default absent: mzLib's runLevelGroup default, null, one group of every site; range category | modification. With remove-run-level only. Whose run level applies to a site: category, one level per modification category (mzLib's ModificationSite.Category); or modification, one level per modification name. A pair within one group is correlated given that group's level, a pair across two groups given both. Not with run-level-groups.

run_level_groups (wire --run-level-groups)

path; default absent. With remove-run-level only. A TSV with a header row, then modification, group: one row per modification name, mapping it to its group, for example every phosphorylation to phospho. Every modification among the sites needs a group. The wire form of mzLib's runLevelGroup for any grouping, such as chemistry. Not with run-level-group.

Returned fields

Each field with its type, its unit, and what NA means when it is NA.

observations_file

string; never NA. Absolute path of the observations table.

samples_file

string; NA when no --samples: pairs are across runs. Absolute path of the run-to-sample table.

type

string; never NA. physical, covarying or both, as asked.

observation_count

int; in rows; never NA. Observation rows read.

run_count

int; in runs; never NA. Distinct runs in the observations.

sample_count

int; in samples; NA when no --samples. Distinct samples in the run-to-sample table.

run_names

string[]; never NA. The runs, or with --samples the samples, the pairs were computed over, in ordinal order.

covarying_run_count

int; in runs; NA when type physical: no co-varying pairs computed. The runs (or samples) where any site was identified or covered: the denominator of min_quantified_fraction.

min_quantified_fraction

float; in fraction of the runs (0 to 1); NA when type physical. The guard used: as given, or mzLib's default.

exclude_ceiling

bool; NA when type physical, or covarying without --keep-ceiling (mzLib decided). false with --keep-ceiling. Null when the caller did not choose: mzLib's CoVarying resolved its nullable excludeCeiling itself (since mzLib #1468), and the bridge does not restate that rule to name the value.

include_bounds

bool; NA when type physical. Whether one-form cells entered as tied bounds: true with --include-bounds, else mzLib's default (false).

min_untied_share

float; in fraction of the shared runs (0 to 1); NA when bounds were not included (or type physical). mzLib's PtmPairEngine.MinUntiedShare: with bounds, a pair is tested only if one of its sites has at least this share of the shared runs outside its largest tie of bounds.

run_covariate_file

string; NA when no --run-covariate. Absolute path of the run covariate table.

run_covariate_name

string; NA when no --run-covariate. The covariate's name: the run covariate table's second header.

run_covariate_runs_missing

string[]; NA when no --run-covariate. Runs (or samples) of covarying_run_count with no value in the run covariate table, in ordinal order: mzLib left them out of every pair. Empty when every run has one.

remove_run_level

bool; NA when type physical. Whether co-varying pairs were correlated given the run level.

run_level_group

string; NA when the run level was not removed (or type physical). none (one group of every site, mzLib's default), category, modification, or file (--run-level-groups).

run_level_groups_file

string; NA when no --run-level-groups. Absolute path of the modification-to-group table.

min_runs_for_run_level

int; in runs; NA when neither the run level nor a run covariate was removed. mzLib's PtmPairEngine.MinRunsForRunLevel: with the run level or a run covariate removed, a pair sharing fewer runs (with a level, and a covariate value) is not tested, test_status too_few_shared_runs.

min_sites_for_run_level

int; in sites; NA when the run level was not removed. mzLib's PtmPairEngine.MinSitesForRunLevel: a run whose group has fewer other sites with a value there has no level.

modifications

string[]; NA when no --modifications filter. The modification names the sites were limited to.

categories

string[]; NA when no --categories filter. The categories the sites were limited to.

ignored_columns

string[]; never NA. Columns of the observations file that were not read; empty when every column was read.

physical_count

int; in pairs; NA when type covarying. Physical pairs found.

covarying_count

int; in pairs; NA when type physical. Co-varying pairs tested or reported.

row_count

int; in rows; never NA. Pairs in the table.

column_names

string[]; never NA. The table's columns, in order.

records (wire columns)

table; never NA. One row per pair, physical first, each type in mzLib's order (by site_a, then site_b).

caveats

string[]; never NA. What each pair type means for the types computed, the bounds when included, and the run level or the run covariate when removed; plus one with --samples, one listing runs with no covariate value, one when columns were not read, and one counting untested pairs by test_status when there are any.

Columns of records

result_type

string; never NA. physical (mzLib's PairResultType P: both modifications identified on one peptidoform, so on one molecule) | covarying (type A: occupancies correlated across runs).

site_a

string; never NA. The first site's key, as ptmqtl occupancy's site_key; ordinally before site_b. A pair is written once.

site_b

string; never NA. The second site's key.

same_protein

bool; never NA. Both sites on the same protein accession.

overlapping

bool; never NA. Some peptide covers both sites: one span on one protein, or one peptide (by base sequence) mapped to both proteins. Always true for physical. A co-varying overlapping pair shares peptides, so it is correlated by construction, and is left out of its family's adjustment.

statistic

float; in physical: fraction (0 to 1), co-occupancy; covarying: unitless correlation (-1 to 1); NA when physical: never quantified together in any run; covarying: not tested (test_status). physical: median over runs of the co-occupancy, the intensity of peptidoforms carrying both modifications over the intensity of peptidoforms covering both positions. covarying: Spearman's rho of the two occupancies across runs; with the run level or a run covariate removed, the partial rho given them.

p_value

float; in fraction (0 to 1); NA when physical (no test in this mzLib), or not tested (test_status). Two-sided Spearman p-value against rho = 0, computed as spearman_method says.

q

float; in fraction (0 to 1); NA when not in the family: physical, overlapping, or not tested (test_status). Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p within fdr_family, over that family's non-overlapping tested pairs. Not a target-decoy q-value.

fdr_family

string; never NA. The family the adjustment runs over, mzLib's PtmPair.FdrFamily verbatim: P or A (physical or co-varying), then intra (same protein) or inter, for example A:inter.

n

int; in runs; never NA. physical: runs where a doubly modified peptidoform was identified. covarying: runs where both sites have a value (with include-bounds, a value or a bound) and every covariate removed is known there (the run level, the run covariate).

statistic_n

int; in runs; never NA. Runs statistic was computed on. physical: runs where the doubly modified form and the forms covering both positions were quantified, at most n. covarying: equal to n.

spearman_method

string; NA when physical: no correlation. exact (the full permutation distribution, for 9 or fewer runs without ties, plain only) | asymptotic (t on n - 2 degrees of freedom, or n - 2 - k given k covariates: the run level, one or two for a pair across groups, less any level the other carries entirely, and the run covariate) | not_estimable (the pair was not tested, for the reason test_status gives).

run_level_removed

bool; never NA. Whether statistic and p_value are the partial correlation given the run level. Always false for physical.

test_status

string; NA when physical: no test. mzLib's PairTestStatus (#1468): tested (statistic, p_value and q, unless overlapping, are set) | not_estimable (too few complete runs, a site constant over them, or a covariate that carries a site entirely) | too_few_shared_runs (partial on the run level or a run covariate, on fewer than min_runs_for_run_level runs) | both_sites_mostly_bounds (with include-bounds, neither site has min_untied_share of the shared runs outside its largest tie).

bounds_included

bool; never NA. Whether one-form cells entered as tied bounds (include-bounds). Always false for physical.

run_covariate_removed

bool; never NA. Whether statistic and p_value are partial given the run covariate. Always false for physical.

Errors

Each is an R condition carrying the class shown and mzlib_error; see mzlib_error.

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

observations missing, blank or not found; type missing or not physical, covarying or both; samples or run-level-groups given without a value or not found; modifications and categories both given, or either blank

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

min-quantified-fraction, keep-ceiling, include-bounds, run-covariate, remove-run-level, run-level-group or run-level-groups with type physical; run-level-group or run-level-groups without remove-run-level; both of them; run-level-group other than category or modification; min-quantified-fraction not above 0 and at most 1, or not a number; keep-ceiling, include-bounds or remove-run-level written with a value; run-covariate given without a value or not found

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

a table malformed as ptmqtl occupancy describes; the run-level-groups file without two fields per row, with a blank or repeated modification, or with no group for a modification among the sites; the run-covariate file without a two-field header, with a row not of two fields, an empty or repeated run, a value that is not a number, or no runs

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

mzLib refuses the run covariate, in its own words: a value that is not finite (blank, NA or NaN included)

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

mzLib refuses the observations, in its own words, as ptmqtl occupancy lists

mzlib_bridge_error (correctness)

never expected

mzlib_service_unavailable (service_unavailable)

Never raised by this verb.

Caveats

  • physical: both modifications on one peptidoform, so on one molecule. statistic is the median co-occupancy over the statistic_n runs where both were quantified. There is no test in this mzLib: p_value and q are null.

  • covarying: Spearman's rho across runs on the runs where both sites are quantified. Floors and not_detected cells are not values and are left out, and so, unless keep-ceiling, are ceilings. With include-bounds they enter as tied bounds instead: low (not_detected, floor) below every fraction, high (a ceiling, or count_only seen only modified) above.

  • A site enters co-varying pairs only if quantified (with include-bounds, a value or a bound) in at least min_quantified_fraction of covarying_run_count, rounded up.

  • With include-bounds, a pair whose two sites are both mostly one bound (less than min_untied_share of the shared runs outside each site's largest tie) is not tested: mzLib's simulation found Spearman's t test then calls 2 to 5 times too many pairs at p < 0.001 with no relation (PtmPairEngine.MinUntiedShare).

  • With run-covariate, rho is partial given the covariate, ranked like every variable. A run with no value is left out of every pair, and a pair sharing fewer than min_runs_for_run_level runs is too_few_shared_runs.

  • q is Benjamini-Hochberg within fdr_family. An overlapping pair is reported with q null: shared peptides correlate it by construction. q is not a target-decoy q-value.

  • With remove-run-level, a run's level is the median occupancy there of the other tested sites of the pair's group; a run with fewer than min_sites_for_run_level such sites has no level, and a pair sharing fewer than min_runs_for_run_level runs with a level is not_estimable (the partial test's t on n - 3 df is too liberal there). Use it for a batch or loading shift only: where the run level follows the design, it removes the effect under study.

  • The observations follow ptmqtl occupancy's rules and exclusions: MS/MS identifications only, one row per (run, peptidoform, protein).

Performance

Every call starts one bridge process, which costs a .NET start-up before any work.

Same verb in other bindings

  • Python (pyMzLib): pymzlib.ptmqtl.pairs

  • Rust (mzLibRust): mzlib::ptmqtl::pairs_with with PairsOptions

  • R (mzLibR): ptmqtl_pairs

Since

Wire protocol 1; pyMzLib 0.6.0; mzLibRust 0.1.0; mzLibR 0.1.0.

References

  • doi:10.2307/1412159: the rank correlation coefficient rho of co-varying pairs (Spearman, Am J Psychol 15:72, 1904)

  • doi:10.5351/CSAM.2015.22.6.665: ppcor, whose pcor.test(method = 'spearman') the partial correlation given the run level reproduces (Kim, Commun Stat Appl Methods 22:665, 2015)

  • doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1995.tb02031.x: the step-up adjustment behind q, within each fdr_family (Benjamini and Hochberg, J R Stat Soc B 57:289, 1995)

See also

ptmqtl_occupancy, stats_correlate

Examples


# Two modifications on one molecule, mzLib's PhysicalPairsCarryCoOccupancy case:
cases <- system.file("extdata", "ptmqtl", "cases.tsv", package = "mzLibR")
found <- ptmqtl_pairs(cases, type = "physical")
found$records[, c("site_a", "statistic", "n", "statistic_n", "p_value")]
#>                                              site_a statistic n statistic_n
#> 1 TWO_ON_ONE:K14:Common Biological:Acetylation on K      0.25 2           1
#>   p_value
#> 1      NA

# Twelve runs in two batches, every site 0.2 higher in the second. The batch alone correlates
# two sites; given each run's level, they are unrelated:
batch <- system.file("extdata", "ptmqtl", "batch.tsv", package = "mzLibR")
plain <- ptmqtl_pairs(batch, type = "covarying")
given <- ptmqtl_pairs(batch, type = "covarying", remove_run_level = TRUE)
pick <- function(r) r$statistic[startsWith(r$site_a, "PAIR_S") & startsWith(r$site_b, "PAIR_T")]
round(c(plain = pick(plain$records), given = pick(given$records)), 2)
#> plain given 
#>  0.76  0.03 

# Two sites with a value in six of ten runs and a bound in the rest (mzLib's
# BoundsEnterTypeAAsTiedRanks). Six is below mzLib's 70% guard, so no pair is tested until the
# bounds enter:
bounds <- system.file("extdata", "ptmqtl", "bounds.tsv", package = "mzLibR")
ptmqtl_pairs(bounds, type = "covarying")$row_count
#> [1] 0
bounded <- ptmqtl_pairs(bounds, type = "covarying", include_bounds = TRUE)
bounded$records[, c("n", "test_status", "bounds_included")]
#>   n test_status bounds_included
#> 1 9      tested            TRUE
